page: Amazon Web Services c7g.medium is a compute-optimized cloud server built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. It utilizes an AWS Neoverse-V1 Graviton processor running at 2.6 GHz, providing 1 dedicated physical core mapped directly to 1 vCPU with a single thread. The instance incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. System memory totals 2.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation. There are no local storage disks bundled with the hardware, requiring EBS volumes for persistent storage, and no hardware GPUs are attached. Network connectivity is configured with a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight capable single-threaded capabilities alongside strict single-core resource ceilings. In Geekbench testing, the single-core rating reaches 1380.0, placing it in the median range among cloud hardware, while stress-ng single-core performance registers 1505.29. However, aggregate multi-core throughput mirrors the single-core ceiling, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 763.05 and lower multi-core ratings across system tasks. Memory read operations achieve 28.44 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks, while write throughput measures 10.44 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput records 1.61 million operations per second, and static web serving reaches 1.87 GB/sec.

The qualitative efficiency of the hardware profile stems from dedicated core execution without hyperthreading overhead, ensuring consistent execution times for lightweight processes. Memory and CPU density are constrained, meaning the instance is ill-suited for parallel compiling, large in-memory caches, or data processing pipelines. It is best deployed as a lightweight execution target for background jobs, microservices, small API proxies, continuous integration build agents, and ARM-native application testing.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.medium is a compute-optimized entry-level cloud instance powered by an arm64 AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU paired with 2.0 GB of memory and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no local storage or hardware accelerators, depending entirely on remote block storage. Benchmark assessments show competitive single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 1380.0 and stress-ng score of 1505.29, placing single-threaded compute within the middle tier of comparable instances. Aggregate throughput is naturally restricted by the single-core configuration and modest 2.0 GB memory envelope. Consequently, the instance offers an efficient, predictable compute environment for microservices, lightweight web routing, continuous integration workers, and small-scale arm64 development workloads where multi-threaded scale and local storage are unnecessary.
